In The Supreme Court Of India

 (@ Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No. 5248/2025)
 Gourav ...Appe
 Versus
 State Of Haryana .Respo
 O R D E R
Leave granted.
This appeal challenges the order dated 19.02.2025 passed by the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh in CRM-M-62592-2024.

entities.text: High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Apprehending arrest in connection with crime registered pursuant to FIR No. 733 of 2023 lodged with P.S. Bhiwani Sadar, District Bhiwani, Haryana in respect of the offences punishable under Sections 323, 34, 376, 379A and 506 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC for short), the appellant preferred an application before the High Court seeking anticipatory bail in terms of Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023(BNSS for short).
The application for anticipatory bail having been rejected by the High Court vide the impugned order dated 19.02.2025, the instant appeal has been preferred.

By order dated 04.03.2025, this Court passed the following order:
1.

It is submitted by the learned senior counsel, Mr. Rishi Malhotra, appearing for the petitioner that though, the impugned order was dictated by the High Court on 19.02.2025, neither the certified copy of the said order is available nor it has been uploaded on the website of the concerned High Court, due to which, he has not been able to produce the same on record.
2. The concerned High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh is requested to upload the said order immediately.

entities.text: High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. List the matter on 07.03.2025.

In the meantime, till the next date of hearing, in the event of arrest of the petitioner, in connection with the F.I.R. No. 733 dated 28.11.2023, registered at Police Station- Bhiwani, Sadarand, for the offence punishable under Sections 323,376,379A, 506 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, he shall be released on bail, if not required in any other case, on such terms and conditions that may be imposed or deem fit by the Trial Court and also subject to his joining the investigation diligently.
Thereafter, when the matter again came for hearing on 01.04.2025, this Court passed the following order:
1.It appears that though, the Court had passed order on 04.03.2025, the notice was not issued to the respondent  State.
2.Application seeking permission to file SLP without certified/plain copy of the impugned order is granted.
3. Let the notice be issued, returnable after two weeks.
4. Interim order granted earlier to continue till the next date of hearing. We have heard learned senior counsel in support of the appellant and learned counsel for the respondent(s)/State.
Learned senior counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant has co-operated with the investigation and the charge sheet has also been filed.
In fact, the relationship between the appellant and the so-called victim was actually a consensual one; that false and frivolous allegations have been made as against the appellant herein.

He submitted that by order dated 04.03.2025, this Court granted interim protection and therefore, the said order may be made absolute and relief may be granted to the appellant by setting aside the impugned order.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State submitted that the allegations as against the appellant are serious and there is no merit in this appeal.
Considering the circumstances on record, in our view, the appellant is entitled to the relief claimed under Section 482 of BNSS.
We, therefore, allow this appeal and set aside the order passed by the High Court dated 19.02.2025.

We direct that in the event of arrest of the appellant, the Arresting Officer shall release the appellant on bail subject to furnishing cash security in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty-Five Thousand only) with two like sureties.
It is directed that the appellant shall extend complete cooperation in the ensuing trial.
The appellant shall not misuse his liberty and shall not in any way influence the witnesses or tamper with the material on record.
With the aforesaid directions, the criminal appeal is allowed.
